party_reuse_justification: Reused the prior run's manifest unchanged. The previous receipt recorded no weakness and no legality problem; every member's source map precedes Route 119 in book play order per the manifest's availability_audit, so it remains chronologically legal for this battle.

level_verification.expected_rule: resolved level == cap + current authored offset - 2 (Medium)
level_verification.result: PASS - all four resolved levels equal 48 + offset - 2; driver reported level_cap 48.

attempts.why: Mega Charizard Y evolved on turn 1; its Drought sun-boosted Heat Wave OHKOed Staraptor and Farfetch'd together. Turn 2 a second sun Heat Wave OHKOed Kilowattrel and Unfezant together. Two spread attacks ended the trainer.

strategy_checks.check: TAILWIND flag is backed - Staraptor or Unfezant actually sets Tailwind
strategy_checks.evidence: Staraptor's latched turn-1 choice was Brave Bird, not Tailwind, and it was KOed before executing. Unfezant entered on turn 2 and was KOed before acting. Tailwind was not set at any point in either the original run or this rerun. At +1 the Tailwind lead still does not survive one spread Fire attack.

strategy_checks.check: Farfetch'd Feint is used only to open a shield for a partner's useful hit
strategy_checks.evidence: Farfetch'd's latched turn-1 choice was Brave Bird; it was KOed before acting. No empty Feint observed.

strategy_checks.check: Volt Absorb Kilowattrel is deployed as the Electric answer
strategy_checks.evidence: Kilowattrel entered on turn 2 and chose Thunderbolt into Mega Charizard Y (2x on Fire/Flying) - the correct target. It executed the attack and then fell to the same turn's Heat Wave.

strategy_checks.check: Defiant Farfetch'd converts an opposing Intimidate into an Attack boost
strategy_checks.evidence: Party carried no Intimidate, exactly as the crack line recommends.
Turn 0 state: Charizard and Togekiss both at atk -1 from Staraptor's Intimidate.

protect_summary: Zero opposing Protects. All four members carry Protect and none used one, but neither side reached a second decision point against a live opponent, so there is no basis to call this poor guarding.
ai_notes: Opponent decision time peaked at 0.603 s (36 frames), inside the 1.2 s budget.
Every latched opponent choice observed was an attack at a legal, sensible target. Nothing nonsensical occurred; the trainer simply never got a full turn.

level_changes.reason: Zero-faint, two-turn first-attempt win. Farfetch'd is one of the two joint-lowest bodies at offset 0 and had its full +/-2 budget unspent (the earlier pass raised only Staraptor). +1 is the correct minimum step under the review rule.
Same trigger, same band. Kilowattrel is the only member that landed an attack in either run and is the authored Electric answer; one more level is the cheapest way to buy it a second turn.

level_change_rationale: Won on the first attempt in two turns with zero player faints, which is squarely the +1 review trigger. I deliberately did not raise Staraptor again: it is already at +1 total (from -1) after the previous pass, and the honest finding from both runs is that a single spread Fire attack under self-made sun removes any member of this trainer regardless of level, so spending the last of Staraptor's budget would buy nothing. Farfetch'd and Kilowattrel were both untouched at offset 0 and each takes +1, well inside the +/-2 cap.
could_this_be_cooler: The previous pass's answer stands and this rerun sharpens it: four Flying types with a shared Rock/Electric weakness, and now demonstrably a shared Fire weakness too, means one spread attack from one Pokemon ends the trainer in two turns. Levels cannot fix a four-way shared weakness. The concrete suggestion is unchanged - swap base Farfetch'd for Farfetch'd-Galar (Fighting, Leek + Focus Energy), which keeps the bird-keeper theme, preserves the Defiant-adjacent flavour, and breaks the mono-Flying wall so a single spread move stops being a whole answer. Flagged, not changed.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem. All four members, abilities, items and moves resolved as authored in the work/agent-battle-build-5 ROM.
driver_note: Driver note: per-turn `damage`/`faints` are keyed by Pokemon identity (player:N / opponent_a:N) as of the mid-session driver update, and `occupant_changed` names slots that changed hands. All HP figures in this receipt were read from `state` and from battle text, not from slot-keyed per-turn damage arithmetic, so none of them depend on the old unreliable representation.
